bill.title: To reauthorize the Young Women’s Breast Health Education and Awareness Requires Learning Young Act of 2009.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
bill.officialSummary: This bill reauthorizes and revises programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) that support services and education addressing breast and cervical cancer. The bill reauthorizes through FY2030 and makes changes to the CDC’s National Breast and Cervical Cancer Early Detection Program. This program provides grants to states for breast and cervical cancer screening, diagnostic, and treatment services for individuals who have low incomes, are uninsured, or otherwise lack access to such services. The bill increases flexibility in how states may spend grant funds under the program. The Government Accountability Office must report to Congress on the work of the National Breast and Cervical Cancer Early Detection Program, including the number of individuals served and barriers to accessing screenings. Also, the bill reauthorizes through FY2031 CDC programs relating to young women’s awareness of breast health and breast cancer. These programs include campaigns to educate young women and health care professionals, research on preventing breast cancer in younger women, and grants for resources and services to young women diagnosed with breast cancer and precancerous conditions.

classification.plainSummary: This bill extends federal funding through 2030–2031 for Centers for Disease Control and Prevention programs that help low-income and uninsured women access breast and cervical cancer screening and treatment. It gives states more flexibility in how they spend grant money and requires a government report on how many people are served and what barriers prevent access. The bill also continues education campaigns and research focused on breast cancer in younger women.

industries.rationale: The bill funds screening, diagnostic, and treatment services that hospitals and health systems deliver to low-income patients.
The bill supports diagnostic testing and treatment services for breast and cervical cancer, which involve medical devices and pharmaceuticals.
The program targets uninsured individuals, potentially affecting the pool of patients who might otherwise seek coverage or remain uninsured.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would renew and change programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention that support services and education addressing breast and cervical cancer.
plain.whoItTouches: People with cancer, and the people caring for them.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in treatment and screening. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
